newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin sees no bid problems with insurance ban.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin sees no bid problems with insurance ban.

text.p: Bidding on a $30 million general obligation Wisconsin bond issue Wednesday was not affected by the state's unusual ban on bond insurance, according to a state official.
Frank Hoadley, Wisconsin's capital finance director, said that four bids were recieved for the issue and all were lower than the state expected.

Hoadley said staff will recommend to the state building commission at its meeting Wednesday afternoon the issue be awarded to Prudential Securities, which had the lowest true interest cost bid of 5.93 percent.

Hoadley said that based on aggressive assumptions, taking into consideration the pricing of previous bond sales and market conditions as of Tuesday, a TIC of 6.04 percent had been anticipated for the housing bonds, which are subject to the alternative minimum tax.
"This has come in stronger than we expected even in normal conditions," he said.

And the $30 million bond issue was anything but normal. The official notice of sale for the deal informed underwriters that the successful bidder would have to certify that neither they nor any member of its syndicate obtained insurance for the deal.

Hoadley has said he inserted what many believed was a first-of-its-kind prohibition because he believed the bonds could sell just as well uninsured and that the state would face a higher spread for the deal if underwriters added insurance.
He said he discussed the insurance provision ahead of time with potential bidders and that no one appeared to drop out of bidding as a result of the ban.
Other bidding syndicates were J.P. Morgan Securities, Goldman, Sachs & Co., and Lehman Brothers, according to Hoadley.
Under the state's provision however, insuring the bonds in the secondary market or with portfolio insurance is not prohibited.
